les: Niks leef op sy eie nie
kaps_punt: Inter-afhanklikheid - plante en diere is afhanklik van mekaar; hulle is ook afhanklik van beskikbare hulpbronne (soos lug, water, grond, kos, en plekke om weg te kruip) in hulle eie habitat

items.bewering: Voëls bou neste in die takke, en insekte vreet aan die blare. Al hierdie diere kry by die boom iets wat hulle nodig het.
items.blok: Wat by een boom gebeur
items.bron: Indiana DNR, Mourning Dove fact sheet (https://www.in.gov/dnr/fish-and-wildlife/files/WMFS_Mourning_Dove.pdf): nests of twigs in the crotches of tree limbs; insects feeding on leaves of shrubs and trees, grasshopper diet summaries (weak sources, but uncontested). Volledig in hierdie ronde nagegaan.

items.bewering: 'n Koei in 'n kamp langs die pad vreet aan die gras. 'n Sprinkaan vreet blare, en 'n aap eet vrugte van 'n boom.
items.blok: Diere kry kos by plante
items.bron: Vervet monkey diet: Kruger Park (https://krugerpark.co.za/africa_vervet_monkey.html) and Durham University primate page (https://rahill.webspace.durham.ac.uk/primates/): fruit, flowers, leaves, with insects as a supplement. Grasshoppers: plant-feeders on grasses and leaves of shrubs and trees (several summaries, none contradicting). Cattle as grazers is uncontested.

items.bewering: Sonder daardie plante sou hierdie diere die grootste deel van hulle kos verloor.
items.blok: Diere kry kos by plante
items.bron: Same sources as above: cattle eat only plants, grasshoppers eat almost only plants, and vervet monkeys are 'mainly vegetarian', with insects, eggs and the like as a supplement (Kruger Park; sa-venues.com vervet page). 'Die grootste deel' holds for all three animals named.

items.bewering: 'n Voël bou sy nes van klein takkies hoog in 'n groot boom.
items.blok: Plante gee diere 'n plek om te bly
items.bron: Indiana DNR, Mourning Dove fact sheet (https://www.in.gov/dnr/fish-and-wildlife/files/WMFS_Mourning_Dove.pdf): nests of loosely fitted twigs in the crotches of tree limbs, usually 10-25 feet up. It is given as an example of one bird ('n voël), not as a rule for all birds, so it holds.

items.bewering: 'n Muis maak sy gat onder die wortels van 'n digte bos.
items.blok: Plante gee diere 'n plek om te bly
items.bron: Four-striped grass mouse (Rhabdomys): Wikipedia summary and Fernkloof Nature Reserve profile (https://www.fernkloof.org.za/index.php/ecology/mammals/item/four-striped-grass-mouse): digs burrows with entrances hidden among vegetation, and prefers fairly dense cover. Burrowing under a dense bush fits this as an example of one mouse. No source names roots specifically, but the sentence does not claim this is what every mouse does.

items.bewering: Klein visse kruip weg tussen die riete aan die kant van 'n dam.
items.blok: Plante gee diere 'n plek om te bly
items.bron: Michigan State University Extension, 'Aquatic plants provide shelter for young fish' (https://www.canr.msu.edu/news/aquatic_plants_provide_shelter_for_young_fish): vegetated shallows held 10-100 times more young fish, which use the plants as a refuge from predators; FAO text (https://www.fao.org/4/X7580E/X7580E06.htm): small forage fish and juveniles use vegetated habitats as a refuge.

items.bewering: Baie plante het diere nodig vir stuifmeel (opskrif)
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir stuifmeel
items.bron: Ollerton, Winfree & Tarrant 2011, Oikos (https://pure.northampton.ac.uk/en/publications/how-many-flowering-plants-are-pollinated-by-animals/): about 87.5% of flowering plant species are pollinated by animals; 'New calculations indicate that 90% of flowering plant species are animal-pollinated' (2023, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10517183/): about 90%. 'Baie' is, if anything, an understatement.

items.bewering: 'n By sit op 'n blom en drink die soet sap daarin. Fyn stuifmeel plak intussen aan sy harige lyf vas. By die volgende blom vryf die by 'n bietjie daarvan af.
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir stuifmeel
items.bron: University of Arizona CALES, Africanized honey bee information sheet 4 (https://cales.arizona.edu/pubs/insects/ahb/inf4.html): bees gather nectar for energy, and pollen grains catch in their branched body hairs as they move from flower to flower; some of this pollen rubs off on the next flower of the same species.

items.bewering: Die stuifmeel help eers wanneer dit by die vroulike deel van dieselfde soort plant kom.
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir stuifmeel
items.bron: University of Arizona CALES sheet (above): pollen rubs off onto flowers of the same species, and pollen that lands on the stigma (the female part) starts fertilisation. Pollen of a different species generally does not fertilise.

items.bewering: Baie plante maak eers sade nadat stuifmeel so by hulle aangekom het.
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir stuifmeel
items.bron: Ollerton et al. 2011 and PMC10517183 (above): most flowering plants depend on animal pollination; seed only forms after pollination and fertilisation (UF/IFAS and the botany sources under the pine item). The quantifier 'baie' is correct; apomixis is a rare exception that 'baie' already allows for.

items.bewering: Party plante se stuifmeel waai met die wind van blom tot blom.
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir stuifmeel
items.bron: PMC10517183 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10517183/): the roughly 10% of flowering plants that are not animal-pollinated are mainly wind-pollinated (with a few pollinated by water).

items.bewering: By ander plante bly die stuifmeel binne een blom.
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir stuifmeel
items.bron: Boundless biology on Mendel's peas (https://rachel.core2learn.org/modules/en-boundless-static/www.boundless.com/definition/self-pollination/index.html): pea ovules are fertilised by pollen from the same flower, and the petals stay sealed until pollination has happened (autogamy).

items.bewering: 'n Denneboom het geen blomme nie, en sy stuifmeel waai uit klein manlike keëls. Daardie stuifmeel moet by 'n vroulike keël van 'n denneboom kom.
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir stuifmeel
items.bron: Iowa State University Extension, 'Flowering of Conifers' (https://yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu/article/1993/6-9-1993/conflow.html) and UF/IFAS Pinellas Extension (https://blogs.ifas.ufl.edu/pinellasco/?p=9199): pines have no true flowers; male cones release pollen, which the wind carries, and the scales of receptive female cones open to take it in. Note: strictly, the pollen has to reach a female cone of the same species. 'Van 'n denneboom' is fine at this grade, but it is looser than the 'dieselfde soort plant' used for flowers in the same block.

items.bewering: 'n Voël pik aan 'n ryp vrug en sluk die klein sade in. Hy vlieg ver weg en los die sade in sy mis op 'n nuwe plek.
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir hulle sade
items.bron: University of Coimbra study of 926 wild birds (https://baes.uc.pt/handle/10316/25247): seeds from fleshy fruits are dispersed through the gut (endozoochory), and migrating birds are important long-distance seed dispersers.

items.bewering: Party plante se sade waai weg sonder enige dier se hulp.
items.blok: Baie plante het diere nodig vir hulle sade
items.bron: Michigan State University Extension, 'Wind is essential to natural processes' (https://www.canr.msu.edu/news/wind_is_essential_to_natural_processes): anemochory is seed dispersal by wind (milkweed, maple, cattail, dandelion).

items.bewering: Die by kry kos by die blom, en die blom kry hulp met sy stuifmeel. Hierdie hulp na albei kante toe noem ons inter-afhanklikheid.
items.blok: Inter-afhanklikheid
items.bron: LibreTexts/CK-12, 'Interdependence of Living Things' (https://bio.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Introductory_and_General_Biology/Book%3A_Introductory_Biology_(CK-12)/01%3A_Introduction_to_Biology/1.06%3A_Interdependence_of_Living_Things): species depend on each other, and plants depend on pollinators while pollinators depend on plants for food. Bee and flower is a correct example of mutual dependence.

items.bewering: Diere het plante nodig, en baie plante het ook diere nodig.
items.blok: Inter-afhanklikheid
items.bron: NOAA Ocean Explorer, 'Chemosynthetic Food Web' (https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/edu/learning/5_chemosynthesis/activities/hydrothermal.html) and University of Hawai'i, Exploring Our Fluid Earth (https://manoa.hawaii.edu/exploringourfluidearth/biological/aquatic-plants-and-algae/energy-acquisition/weird-science-hydrothermal-vents-and-cold-seeps): the food webs of animals at hydrothermal vents rest on chemosynthetic bacteria, not on plants. In the sea, most food chains begin with algae, which are not plants. Because the second half of the sentence is qualified ('baie plante') and the first is not ('Diere'), the sentence reads as ALL animals, and that is not true without exception. On land the claim holds through food chains.
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier on the first half so that it holds without exception, for example 'Byna alle diere het plante nodig, en baie plante het ook diere nodig.' Keep the subject and the second half as they are.

items.bewering: Sonder diere sou baie plante nie sade kon maak of versprei nie.
items.blok: Inter-afhanklikheid
items.bron: Ollerton et al. 2011 (pollination, about 87.5% of flowering plants) and University of Coimbra endozoochory study (seed dispersal), both cited above. 'Baie' is correctly qualified.

items.bewering: Elke plant en elke dier bly op 'n plek wat ons sy habitat noem.
items.blok: Alles kom uit hulle eie habitat
items.bron: IPBES glossary (https://ipbes.net/glossary-tag/habitat): a habitat is 'the place or type of site where an organism or population naturally occurs'; InforMEA glossary (https://www.informea.org/en/terms/habitat): 'the locality in which a plant or animal naturally grows or lives'. 'Elke' holds, because it is true by definition.

items.bewering: Die dinge wat 'n habitat gee, word hulpbronne genoem.
items.blok: Alles kom uit hulle eie habitat
items.bron: LibreTexts/CK-12 (above): living things depend on their environment to supply what they need (food, water, shelter); IPBES glossary: habitat also refers to 'the environmental attributes required by a particular species'. A good simplification at this grade.

items.bewering: 'n Plant kan nie opstaan en na 'n beter plek toe stap nie. Alles wat dit nodig het, moet in sy eie habitat wees.
items.blok: Alles kom uit hulle eie habitat
items.bron: University of Minnesota open textbook, 'The Science of Plants', chapter 11 (https://open.lib.umn.edu/horticulture/part/chapter-11-water-and-light): 'Plants are sessile and cannot move to locations that might be more suitable', and they take water and nutrients from where they grow.

items.bewering: Nie elke plant en elke dier het presies dieselfde hulpbronne nodig nie.
items.blok: Alles kom uit hulle eie habitat
items.bron: IPBES glossary (above): the environmental attributes 'required by a particular species', which differ from species to species; the lesson's own list shows it, with a cow and a fish getting oxygen in different ways (see the fish item).

items.bewering: Lug: 'n koei asem die suurstof daarin in, maar 'n vis kry syne uit die water.
items.blok: Wat 'n habitat kan verskaf
items.bron: PetMD, 'How Do Fish Breathe?' (https://www.petmd.com/fish/how-do-fish-breathe): fish take dissolved oxygen from water through their gills, while air-breathing animals take it from the air. A few fish (lungfish and others) also gulp air, but ''n vis' is an example and not a rule.

items.bewering: Water: 'n dier drink uit 'n dam, en 'n plant kry dit uit die grond.
items.blok: Wat 'n habitat kan verskaf
items.bron: University of Minnesota open textbook, chapter 11 (above): plants draw water and nutrients from the soil through their roots. An example sentence, not a rule for every plant.

items.bewering: Grond: dit hou 'n plant se wortels vas, en party diere grawe daarin.
items.blok: Wat 'n habitat kan verskaf
items.bron: University of Minnesota open textbook (above): root systems anchor the plant in the soil; Fernkloof profile of the four-striped grass mouse (above): it digs burrows up to 50 cm deep.

items.bewering: Kos: 'n dier kry sy kos in sy eie habitat.
items.blok: Wat 'n habitat kan verskaf
items.bron: LibreTexts/CK-12 (above): the environment supplies living things with food, water and shelter; IPBES (above) on habitat as the place where an organism naturally occurs.

items.bewering: Plekke om weg te kruip: klippe, gate en digte bosse.
items.blok: Wat 'n habitat kan verskaf
items.bron: Fernkloof and Wikipedia profiles of Rhabdomys (above): burrows (gates) and dense cover used as shelter; MSU Extension (above): dense plants as a refuge. That rocks are shelters is uncontested.

items.bewering: inter-afhanklikheid: Wanneer lewende dinge mekaar nodig het vir kos, skuiling of hulp.
items.blok: begrip: inter-afhanklikheid
items.bron: LibreTexts/CK-12 'Interdependence of Living Things' (above): species in a community depend on one another, for food, shelter and pollination among other things (the ant-acacia example: shelter and food in exchange for protection). The definition is accurate and agrees with the study block's 'hulp na albei kante toe'.

items.bewering: hulpbron: Iets in 'n habitat wat 'n plant of 'n dier nodig het.
items.blok: begrip: hulpbron
items.bron: LibreTexts/CK-12 (above): the environment supplies what living things need; IPBES (above): environmental attributes required by a species. Accurate at this grade.

items.bewering: habitat: Die plek waar 'n plant of 'n dier lewe.
items.blok: begrip: habitat
items.bron: InforMEA glossary (https://www.informea.org/en/terms/habitat): 'the locality in which a plant or animal naturally grows or lives'; IPBES glossary (https://ipbes.net/glossary-tag/habitat).

items.bewering: stuifmeel: Die fyn korreltjies uit 'n blom se manlike deel of 'n manlike keël, wat sade help maak.
items.blok: begrip: stuifmeel
items.bron: Iowa State Extension 'Flowering of Conifers' and the botany sources under the pine item (above): male cones make pollen grains; in flowering plants pollen comes from the anthers (the male part); pollen that reaches an ovule leads to fertilisation and seed formation. The entry is accurate on its own, outside its block.

opsomming: One sentence is too broad: 'Diere het plante nodig' in the block 'Inter-afhanklikheid' leaves its quantifier off while the second half says 'baie plante', so it reads as all animals, and animals at deep-sea vents (and most food chains in the sea, which rest on algae) do not depend on plants. Narrow it to something like 'byna alle diere'. Every other claim was checked against sources and confirmed. The lesson contains no analogies, and its one superlative ('die grootste deel van hulle kos') holds for all three animals named.
